newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD auction set for April 29-minister.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD auction set for April 29-minister.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said he was "fully condident" the sale of mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) would take place April 29 as planned.

"I am fully confident the auction will take place on April 29. I think all the conditions are in place to keep the auction on track for the 29th," Kandir told reporters after a meeting of Brazil's National Monetary Council.
Kandir acknowledged there were several court cases that might yet interfere with the April 29 scheduled auction of 45 percent of voting shares in CVRD.
But he added "the most important problem was overcome yesterday and I see no reason to reschedule the auction."
The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), brazil's highest court, Wednesday rejected a constitutional challenge to the CVRD privatization.
But the court upheld an injunction which suspended the transfer to CVRD of a large section of the Carajas iron ore mining complex in the Amazon region.
Kandir said the injunction did not affect the auction.
"That injunction does not interfere with the enthusiasm of those groups interested in bidding in the auction," he said.

Brazilian financial daily Gazeta Mercantil quoted the president of the Sao Paulo bankers union as denouncing a conflict of interest involving National Development Bank (BNDES) privatization director Jose Pio Borges who holds a seat on the board of directors of pulp and paper producer Aracruz Celulose.
Among companies controlling Aracruz are South African mining giant Anglo American Corp and Brazil's Banco Safra, both of which have joined the Valecom consortium to bid in next Tuesday's auction.
But Kandir, suggesting details should be checked with the BNDES, said he believed Borges held a seat on the Aracruz board as a representative of BNDESpar, the bank's investment wing.
"The strange thing would be if the BNDESpar did not have a representative on the board of a company in which it has put a significant amount of capital," the minister said.
